hook.line: Everyone in the café knows somebody who complains about everything. Spanish has a short way to say how someone spends their time, and it is usually a gentle complaint.
hook.es: Hernando se pasa la vida quejándose.
hook.en: Hernando spends his whole life complaining.

examples.es: Hernando se pasa la vida quejándose.
examples.en: Hernando spends his whole life complaining.

examples.es: Mariana se pasa la vida viajando.
examples.en: Mariana spends her whole life travelling.

examples.es: ¿Te pasas la vida mirando el celular?
examples.en: Do you spend your whole life looking at your phone? (to a friend)

examples.es: Vale se pasó la mañana haciendo pan.
examples.en: Vale spent the morning making bread.

rule:
To say how someone fills their time, use *pasarse* plus a stretch of time plus the *-ando* / *-iendo* form: *me paso*, *te pasas*, *se pasa*, *nos pasamos*.
*La vida* means "all the time" and is exaggeration. Smaller stretches: *el día*, *la tarde*, *la noche*, *la semana*.
Present is a habit or a complaint. The past (*me pasé*) is one stretch that is over.
The activity is the *-ando* / *-iendo* form: no *a*, no *en*, no infinitive.
smallPrint: Teachers call *quejándose* and *durmiendo* gerunds. Here they say what fills the time.

options: He spends his whole life complaining.
He spent the whole day complaining.
He is going to complain all his life.

readAndPick.es: ¿Te pasas la vida mirando el celular?
options: Do you spend your whole life looking at your phone? (to a friend)
Does he spend his whole life looking at his phone?

readAndPick.es: Mariana se pasa la vida viajando.
options: Mariana spends her whole life travelling.

readAndPick.es: Vale se pasó la mañana haciendo pan.
options: Vale spends every morning making bread.
Vale spent the morning making bread.

readAndPick.es: Me paso la vida esperando el bus.
options: I spend my whole life waiting for the bus.
I spent the whole day waiting for the bus.

readAndPick.es: Se pasaron la semana preparando la fiesta.
options: He spent the week preparing the party.
They spend every week preparing the party.
They spent the week preparing the party.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *quejándose* or *quejarse*, then type the whole sentence: Hernando se pasa la vida ___. (Hernando spends his whole life complaining.)
yourTurn.answer: Hernando se pasa la vida quejándose.
yourTurn.why: The activity after the time is the *-ando* / *-iendo* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *durmiendo* or *dormir*, then type the whole sentence: Me pasé el día ___. (I spent the day sleeping.)
yourTurn.why: Again the *-iendo* form, not the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: We spent the night talking.
Type it in Spanish: Mariana spends her whole life travelling.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana se pasa la vida viajando.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Do you spend your whole life looking at your phone? (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Te pasas la vida mirando el celular?

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Vale: *Me paso la mañana haciendo pan.* becomes: Vale spends the morning making bread.
yourTurn.answer: Vale se pasa la mañana haciendo pan.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it past: *Se pasa la tarde leyendo.* becomes: He spent the afternoon reading.
yourTurn.why: One finished afternoon is the past: *pasó*.

pitfalls.wrong: Se pasa la vida a quejarse.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *pasarse* the activity is the *-ando* / *-iendo* form: no *a*, no infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: Me paso el día durmiendo ayer.
pitfalls.right: Ayer me pasé el día durmiendo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Yesterday is over, so *pasé*, not *paso*.
Almost. It is *we* doing it, so the verb is *pasamos*.

personal: Tell me what you spend your weekends doing. Use *me paso el fin de semana…* plus an *-ando* or *-iendo* verb.
